name: Georgian neoclassical manufacture
summary: The household goods of the first English factories: mahogany furniture, creamware and jasperware, ormolu and Sheffield plate, all made in series from the classical models of the architect and the pattern book.

philosophy.core_thesis: A factory can make an object that looks like a work of antiquity: the form comes from the classical model, and the mould, the lathe and the die repeat it with a fine finish.
design_principles: Take each form from a classical model: an urn, a column, a vase or an acanthus leaf.
Use a slim, straight leg with 8 to 12 flutes, or a turned leg with a tapered foot.
Use mahogany with a figured veneer and a fine French polish on all large wood surfaces.
Put the ornament in a narrow band: a bead, a reed, a Greek key or a husk chain of 10 to 25 mm.
Make a thin, cast and gilded metal mount for each handle, sconce and clock case.
Keep a pale ground, such as cream, sage or stone, and one gilded accent for each object.
Draw the form so that a workshop can repeat it with a mould, a lathe or a die.
anti_patterns: Heavy carved scrolls and shells in the rococo manner
Raw machine marks on a visible surface

form.geometry: Straight lines, circles and ovals, with the urn, the column and the arch as the main shapes.
form.silhouette: A light, upright outline on slim legs: a rectangular case with a gentle serpentine or bow front, and a vase or an urn as the top.
form.edges: Crisp edges with a small bead or reed of 3 to 6 mm; no soft or bulbous curves.
form.proportion: A sideboard is about 90 cm high and 180 cm long; a leg is about 1/12 of its height in width; a vase has a height of 1.5 to 2 times its widest diameter.
form.ornament: A band of low relief: a bead, a husk chain, a Greek key, a reed or a laurel wreath, in cast metal, plaster or inlay.
rules: Each object has one classical motif, such as a flute, an urn or a husk chain.
Each leg is straight and tapered, or turned with a round foot.
A band of ornament is 10 to 25 mm wide.
Gilding covers less than 20% of the visible surface.
Each vase or urn has a base, a body and a lid or rim in 3 clear parts.

materials.rule: Mahogany, brass and ceramic carry the object; silk, marble and mirror glass give the fine surfaces; 0% of the visible surface is a modern polymer.

finish.gloss: 60–85 GU on wood and gilding, 80–95 GU on glaze, 15–30 GU on paint
finish.patina: A clean, fine surface in its first state; the style allows a soft, warm age of the wood and the gilding, but not rust or wear.

hardware.section: Rods and stems 10–20 mm; a cast mount 2–4 mm thick
hardware.joints: Hidden joints; cast and chased mounts screwed to the wood; a ring pull on a rose plate.
hardware.handles: A ring pull on a cast rose, a lion mask with a ring, or a small turned knob of wood or porcelain.
hardware.switches_and_taps: Before 1880 there is no electric switch; the period-faithful reissue is a rotary switch in white porcelain with a brass ring. A tap has a swan neck and a cross handle in brass.

palette.strategy: Pale grounds of cream, stone and sage, set against the red-brown of mahogany and the yellow of brass and gilding.

manufacture.scale: Large workshops and early factories of 100 to 300 workers; sets and services made in the hundreds from pattern books.
manufacture.signs: Flutes of equal width, repeated mounts of one casting, and a clear glaze with fine, even thickness.

objects.form: pedestal basin with a marble top
round rotary in white porcelain with a brass ring (a period-faithful reissue)
two-arm sconce with a gilt mount
settee with a straight back and fluted legs
creamware dinner service with a beaded rim
oval pier glass in a gilt frame

positive: oval mirror in a gilt frame
studio product photograph, soft window light

canonical_works.work: Cabinet in the manner of the pattern books

emotion.target_response: Calm pleasure in a refined, ordered object: it looks light, clean and sure of its proportion.

use_cases: period hardware for a Georgian or Regency house
a reissue of a classical lamp or vase
a still life with creamware and mahogany
a hardware schedule for a listed building
avoid_when: The brief asks for a bare, plain or modern object.
The room needs soft, worn and rustic surfaces.

modifiers.how: Remove the flutes and the gilding, and use plain maple and cherry with an oil finish.
Add carved and turned parts, dark polish, velvet and pressed glass.
Keep the slim leg and the light outline, and use pale oak, linen and white ceramic.

era_blend.note: A contemporary reinterpretation keeps the style when it keeps the forms and the materials.
